28300-harper-s-young-people-january-6-18.title: Harper S Young People January 6 1880 An Illustrated Weekly
28300-harper-s-young-people-january-6-18.creator: Unknown
28300-harper-s-young-people-january-6-18.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The little flying-squirrels, the dearest little creatures for pets, are natives of the Rocky Mountains, but are found in all parts of the United States. They are very lazy, and sleep nearly all day, coming out at twilight for a merry frolic, leaping, flying, or scampering at pleasure among the tree-tops. They generally make their nest in some hollow trunk, where it is very difficult to find them.

50556-the-jews.title: The Jews
50556-the-jews.creator: Hilaire Belloc
50556-the-jews.description: A book by Hilaire Belloc. to it and careful of its good--in this latter form it may best be called _Recognition_. The first kind of segregation has often been attempted in history--it has been partially successful over long periods--but has always left behind it a sense of injustice and has not really solved the problem--also it has always failed in the end.

arxiv-1904-11207.title: Exploring Auxiliary Context: Discrete Semantic Transfer Hashing for Scalable Image Retrieval
arxiv-1904-11207.creator: Lei Zhu, Zi Huang, Zhihui Li, Liang Xie, Heng Tao Shen
arxiv-1904-11207.description: Abstract Unsupervised hashing can desirably support scalable content-based image retrieval (SCBIR) for its appealing advantages of semantic label independence, memory and search efficiency. However, the learned hash codes are embedded with limited discriminative semantics due to the intrinsic limitation of image representation.

arxiv-1909-04569.title: Incompleteness Ex Machina
arxiv-1909-04569.creator: Sebastian Oberhoff
arxiv-1909-04569.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Sebastian Oberhoff. In this essay we’ll prove Gödel’s incompleteness theorems twice. First, we’ll prove them the good old-fashioned way. Then we’ll repeat the feat in the setting of computation. In the process we’ll discover that Gödel’s work, rightly viewed, needs to be split into two parts: the transport of computation into the arena of arithmetic on the one hand and the actual incompleteness theorems on the other. After we’re done there will be cake.

arxiv-2107-03260.title: Tracing the dynamical interplay of low-energy reaction processes of exotic nuclei using a two-center molecular continuum
arxiv-2107-03260.creator: Laura Moschini, Alexis Diaz-Torres
arxiv-2107-03260.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Laura Moschini, Alexis Diaz-Torres. The competition among reaction processes of a weakly-bound projectile at intermediate times of a slow collision has been unraveled. This has been done using a two-center molecular continuum within a semiclassical, time-dependent coupled-channel reaction model. Dynamical probabilities of elastic scattering, transfer and breakup agree with those derived from the direct integration of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, demonstrating the usefulness of a two-center molecular continuum for gaining insights into the reaction dynamics of exotic nuclei.

arxiv-2111-11644.title: Neutrino mass spectrum: Present indication and future prospect Preprint: arXiv:xxxx.xxxx [hep-ph]
arxiv-2111-11644.creator: S. Cao, N. T. Hong Van, T. V. Ngoc, P. T. Quyen
arxiv-2111-11644.description: Abstract The fact that neutrinos are massive has been the most crucial evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model of elementary particles. To date, we still do not know how neutrinos get mass and why their mass is much smaller than that of their charged fermion cousins.

arxiv-2201-04871.title: Interface potential and line tension for Bose-Einstein condensate mixtures near a hard wall
arxiv-2201-04871.creator: Bert Van Schaeybroeck, Patrick Navez, Joseph O. Indekeu
arxiv-2201-04871.description: Abstract Within Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) theory we derive the interface potential V ⁡ ( ℓ ) V(\ell) which describes the interaction between the interface separating two demixed Bose-condensed gases and an optical hard wall at a distance ℓ \ell . Previous work revealed that this interaction gives rise to extraordinary wetting and prewetting phenomena.

arxiv-2203-02765.title: Flare echos from relaxation shocks in perturbed relativistic jets
arxiv-2203-02765.creator: G. Fichet de Clairfontaine, Z. Meliani and A. Zech
arxiv-2203-02765.description: Abstract Context. One of the main scenarios to account for the multi-wavelength flux variability observed in relativistic jets of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) is based on diffusive shock acceleration of a population of relativistic electrons on internal shocks of various origins.

arxiv-2207-08943.title: MRCLens: an MRC Dataset Bias Detection Toolkit
arxiv-2207-08943.creator: Yifan Zhong, Haohan Wang, Eric P. Xing
arxiv-2207-08943.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yifan Zhong, Haohan Wang, Eric P. Xing. Many recent neural models have shown remarkable empirical results in Machine Reading Comprehension, but evidence suggests sometimes the models take advantage of dataset biases to predict and fail to generalize on out-of-sample data.

arxiv-2404-16750.title: Hydrodynamics of a Discrete Conservation Law
arxiv-2404-16750.creator: Patrick Sprenger, Christopher Chong, Emmanuel Okyere, Michael Herrmann, P. G. Kevrekidis, Mark A. Hoefer
arxiv-2404-16750.description: Abstract The Riemann problem for the discrete conservation law 2 ​ u ˙ n + u n + 1 2 − u n − 1 2 = 0 2\dot{u}_{n}+u^{2}_{n+1}-u^{2}_{n-1}=0 is classified using Whitham modulation theory, a quasi-continuum approximation, and numerical simulations. A surprisingly elaborate set of solutions to this simple discrete regularization of the inviscid Burgers’ equation is obtained.

arxiv-2504-10094.title: Local-in-time well-posedness for the regular solution to the 2D full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with degenerate viscosities and heat conductivity
arxiv-2504-10094.creator: Yue Cao, Xun Jiang
arxiv-2504-10094.description: Abstract . This paper considers the two-dimensional Cauchy problem of the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with far-field vacuum in ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} , where the viscosity and heat-conductivity coefficients depend on the absolute temperature θ \theta in the form of θ ν \theta^{\nu} with ν > 0 \nu>0 .

arxiv-2504-18407.title: Are We on the Same Page? Examining Developer Perception Alignment in Open Source Code Reviews
arxiv-2504-18407.creator: Yoseph Berhanu Alebachew, Minhyuk Ko, Chris Brown
arxiv-2504-18407.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yoseph Berhanu Alebachew, Minhyuk Ko, Chris Brown. Code reviews are a critical aspect of open-source software (OSS) development, ensuring quality and fostering collaboration. This study examines perceptions, challenges, and biases in OSS code review processes, focusing on the perspectives of Contributors and Maintainers. Through surveys ( n = 289 n=289 ), interviews ( n = 23 n=23 ), and repository analysis ( n = 81 n=81 ), we identify key areas of alignment and disparity.

arxiv-2512-16156.title: Understanding the Neutron Star Population with the SKAO telescopes
arxiv-2512-16156.creator: L. Levin 1, M. Bagchi 2,3, M. Burgay 4, A. T. Deller 5, V. Graber 6, A. Igoshev 7, M. Kramer 8,1, D. Lorimer 9, B. Posselt 10, T. Prabu 11, K. Rajwade 10, N. Rea 12,13, B. Stappers 1, T. M. Tauris 14,8, P. Weltevrede 1, The SKAO Pulsar Science Working Group
arxiv-2512-16156.description: Abstract The known population of non-accreting neutron stars is ever growing and currently consists of more than 3500 sources. Pulsar surveys with the SKAO telescopes will greatly increase the known population, adding radio pulsars to every subgroup in the radio-loud neutron star family.

arxiv-2601-13660.title: Possible time-variable iron-K α \alpha emission in the circumnuclear region of the Circinus galaxy
arxiv-2601-13660.creator: Aiko Miyamoto, \altemailmark \orcid 0009-0009-2127-8830 Taiki Kawamuro, \orcid 0000-0002-6808-2052 Hirokazu Odaka, \orcid 0000-0003-2670-6936 Takuma Izumi, \orcid 0000-0001-9452-0813 and Hironori Matsumoto
arxiv-2601-13660.description: Abstract We present imaging and spatially resolved spectral analyses of eight Chandra data taken for the Circinus galaxy in ≈ \approx 22 years to reveal neutral iron-K α \alpha emission on a circumnuclear scale ( ∼ \sim 10–100 pc) and search for time variability in the emission.

europmc-pmc5701930.creator: Trevethan R.
europmc-pmc5701930.description: Within the context of screening tests, it is important to avoid misconceptions about sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values. In this article, therefore, foundations are first established concerning these metrics along with the first of several aspects of pliability that

plos-pone-0003338.creator: Stéphane Brunet, Julien Dumont, Karen W. Lee et al.
plos-pone-0003338.description: PLOS ONE research article. Formation of female gametes requires acentriolar spindle assembly during meiosis. Mitotic spindles organize from centrosomes and via local activation of the RanGTPase on chromosomes. Vertebrate oocytes present a RanGTP gradient centred on chromatin at all stages of meiotic matura

pmc-10485075.title: Updates to the NASA human system risk management process for space exploration
pmc-10485075.creator: Erik L Antonsen, Erin Connell, Wilma Anton, Robert J Reynolds, Daniel M Buckland, Mary Van Baalen
pmc-10485075.description: This paper describes updates to NASA’s approach for assessing and mitigating spaceflight-induced risks to human health and performance. This approach continues to evolve to meet dynamically changing risk environments: lunar missions are currently being designed and the ultimate destination will be Mars.

pmc-10574454.title: Konjac Glucomannan Counteracted the Side Effects of Excessive Exercise on Gut Microbiome, Endurance, and Strength in an Overtraining Mice Model
pmc-10574454.creator: Yu-Heng Mao, Minghan Wang, Yu Yuan, Jing-Kun Yan, Yanqun Peng, Guoqin Xu, Xiquan Weng, Juan Del Coso
pmc-10574454.description: Excessive exercise without adequate rest can lead to overtraining syndrome, which manifests a series of side effects, including fatigue, gut dysbiosis, and decremental sports performance. Konjac glucomannan (KGM) is a plant polysaccharide with numerous health-improving effects, but few studies reported its effects on the gut microbiome, endurance, and strength in an overtraining model.

pmc-10599262.title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Bipolar II Disorder Treatment: A Case Report
pmc-10599262.creator: Nga N Tran, Sydney Hutto, Landon R Thompson, Aaron Hawkins
pmc-10599262.description: The objective of this case report is to describe and document the use of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to aid in the treatment of bipolar II disorder. A 35-year-old male with a past medical history of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), severe depression, and bipolar II disorder was presented to an outpatient psychiatric clinic 1.

pmc-11435819.title: Cross-Linking Agents in Three-Component Materials Dedicated to Biomedical Applications: A Review
pmc-11435819.creator: Sylwia Grabska-Zielińska, Haw-Ming Huang
pmc-11435819.description: In biomaterials research, using one or two components to prepare materials is common. However, there is a growing interest in developing materials composed of three components, as these can offer enhanced physicochemical properties compared to those consisting of one or two components.

pmc-11479194.title: Finite Element Analysis of Electrostatic Coupling in LISA Pathfinder Inertial Sensors
pmc-11479194.creator: Wenyan Zhang, Jungang Lei, Zuolei Wang, Cunhui Li, Shijia Yang, Jian Min, Xuan Wen, Tomasz Starecki, Piotr Z Wieczorek
pmc-11479194.description: In the LISA Pathfinder (LPF) mission, electrostatic noise can reach the femto-Newtonian level despite the fact that the LPF’s sensors are equipped with potential shielding. Most of the existing simulation studies focus on the electrostatic edge effect and related fields, while the simulation study of the patch effect is neglected.

pmc-11504153.title: Scavenging of Alkylperoxyl Radicals by Addition to Ascorbate: An Alternative Mechanism to Electron Transfer
pmc-11504153.creator: Gabriel Robert, J Richard Wagner, Alessandra Napolitano
pmc-11504153.description: Vitamin C (ascorbate; Asc) is a biologically important antioxidant that scavenges reactive oxygen species such as deleterious alkylperoxyl radicals (ROO•), which are generated by radical-mediated oxidation of biomolecules in the presence of oxygen. The radical trapping proprieties of Asc are conventionally attributed to its ability to undergo single-electron transfers with reactive species.

pmc-11669913.title: Developmental origins of natural sound perception
pmc-11669913.creator: Silvia Polver, Nicole Miller-Viacava, Matthieu Fraticelli, Judit Gervain, Christian Lorenzi
pmc-11669913.description: Infants are exposed to a myriad of sounds early in life, including caregivers' speech, songs, human-made and natural (non-anthropogenic) environmental sounds. While decades of research have established that infants have sophisticated perceptual abilities to process speech, less is known about how they perceive natural environmental sounds.

pmc-12470176.title: A Stratified Analysis of the Associations of Hearing Loss and Allergic Rhinitis with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder in Children: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Korea
pmc-12470176.creator: Bo Ram Yang, Bong Jik Kim
pmc-12470176.description: We conducted a cross-sectional, population-based study to investigate the association between hearing loss and allergic rhinitis with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) using pediatric patient samples from the Korea Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service database (2009–2018). Baseline demographics and the relationships of both conditions with ADHD were analyzed.

pmc-12555358.title: Climate change threatens culturally and regionally relevant physical activities
pmc-12555358.creator: L Grout, C Pirkle, S Schmid, E Yokooji, T Sentell
pmc-12555358.description: BackgroundCulturally or regionally relevant physical activities (CRRPAs), such as traditional sports and games, deliver health benefits to individuals and communities. However, climate change may reduce participation in physical activities, especially those that are ice/snow-based (eg, Nordic skating, Kumoterki races, bandy).

pmc-12650882.title: Integrating Multi-Omics and Medical Imaging in Artificial Intelligence-Based Cancer Research: An Umbrella Review of Fusion Strategies and Applications
pmc-12650882.creator: Ahmed Al Marouf, Jon George Rokne, Reda Alhajj
pmc-12650882.description: Simple SummaryThis study reviews how combining different types of biological data (like genes and proteins) with medical images (such as MRI, CT, or PET scans) can help improve cancer diagnosis and treatment. The authors looked at many review papers published before May 2025 and selected 21 that best fit their goals.

pmc-12654107.title: Inflammatory Semaphorins in the Pathogenesis and Prognosis of Acute Ischemic Stroke
pmc-12654107.creator: Esen Çiçekli, Dilcan Kotan, Levent Avcı
pmc-12654107.description: Background and Objectives: Semaphorins are immunoregulatory proteins involved in inflammation and neurovascular modulation. Their roles in ischemic stroke pathogenesis and prognosis have recently gained attention. This study aimed to evaluate serum levels of semaphorin 3A, 3F, 4A, 4D, and 7A in patients with acute ischemic stroke and investigate their relationship with disease severity and prognosis.

pmc-12666524.title: Correction: Role of the suppressor of cytokine signaling-3 in the pathogenesis of Graves’ orbitopathy
pmc-12666524.creator: Wonjin Kim, Mi-Kyoung Seo, Yong Joon Kim, Soo Hyun Choi, Cheol Ryong Ku, Sangwoo Kim, Eun Jig Lee, Jin Sook Yoon
pmc-12666524.description: lthy individuals (n = 3) were transfected with 20 nM si-SOCS3 or si-con and cultured for 48 h, followed by IL-1β treatment (10 ng/mL) for 1 h, which resulted in an increase in the level of phosphorylated forms of NF-κB and AKT. Protein levels determined using densitometry were normalized to the β-actin levels in the same sample.

pmc-12960417.title: Translational Perspectives on Binge-Eating: Insights from Animal Models
pmc-12960417.creator: Estefania P Azevedo, Sarah A Stern
pmc-12960417.description: Purpose of ReviewBinge-eating is a behavior that is both recognized in both binge-eating disorder and binge-subtypes of restrictive eating disorders. Binge-eating is distinct from obesity, although the two frequently co-occur. The purpose of this review is to examine animal models of binge like behavior independent of obesity as a phenotype and to examine recent findings.

pmc-13161442.title: Curcumin therapeutic potential in gastric cancer prevention, treatment and metastasis suppression
pmc-13161442.creator: Alireza Abdollahi, Samaneh Salarvand, Fereshteh Ameli, Kimia Mozahheb Yousefi, Aysan Nozheh, Zahra Modabber
pmc-13161442.description: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a significant global health burden, characterized by high mortality rates, often due to late-stage diagnosis, resistance to conventional therapies, and metastatic dissemination. This narrative review synthesizes current preclinical and early clinical evidence on the diverse roles of curcumin, a natural polyphenolic compound derived from Curcuma longa (turmeric), in the context of gastric cancer.
